items.stem: Reagan's challenge to Gorbachev was directed at the wall dividing —

choices.text: North and South Korea
North and South Vietnam
East and West Berlin
Israel and Palestine

items.explanation: On June 12, 1987, President Reagan stood at the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin and delivered a direct challenge to Soviet General Secretary Gorbachev: "Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!" The wall in question was the Berlin Wall, the barrier the East German government erected beginning August 13, 1961, to separate communist East Berlin from democratic West Berlin. Choice A is wrong because Reagan's speech was directed at Berlin, not Korea; the Korean Peninsula has never had a single wall dividing its two capitals. Choice B is wrong because Vietnam was already reunified under communist rule by 1975, more than a decade before Reagan spoke. The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, a pivotal moment in the Cold War's end.
items.explanationEs: El 12 de junio de 1987, el presidente Reagan se ubicó en la Puerta de Brandeburgo en Berlín Occidental y lanzó un reto directo al Secretario General soviético Gorbachov: "¡Sr. Gorbachov, derribe este muro!" El muro en cuestión era el Muro de Berlín, la barrera que el gobierno de Alemania Oriental erigió a partir del 13 de agosto de 1961 para separar el comunista Berlín Oriental del democrático Berlín Occidental. La opción A es incorrecta porque el discurso de Reagan se dirigió a Berlín, no a Corea; la Península de Corea nunca ha tenido un solo muro que divida sus dos capitales. La opción B es incorrecta porque Vietnam ya estaba reunificado bajo el gobierno comunista en 1975, más de una década antes de que Reagan hablara. El Muro de Berlín cayó el 9 de noviembre de 1989, un momento decisivo en el fin de la Guerra Fría.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"I am not a crook." — President Richard Nixon, Press Conference, November 17, 1973

In the context of the Watergate scandal, this statement by Nixon was most likely made in response to which of the following?
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento.

"No soy un ladrón." — Presidente Richard Nixon, Conferencia de prensa, 17 de noviembre de 1973

En el contexto del escándalo Watergate, esta declaración de Nixon se hizo más probablemente en respuesta a cuál de los siguientes?

choices.text: Accusations that Nixon had ordered the publication of the Pentagon Papers to embarrass political opponents.
choices.textEs: Acusaciones de que Nixon había ordenado la publicación de los Papeles del Pentágono para perjudicar a sus oponentes políticos.

choices.text: Congressional testimony that Nixon had personally erased 18½ minutes of White House tape recordings.
choices.textEs: El testimonio ante el Congreso de que Nixon había borrado personalmente 18½ minutos de grabaciones de cintas de la Casa Blanca.

choices.text: His announcement that he would resign from the presidency rather than face impeachment.
choices.textEs: Su anuncio de que renunciaría a la presidencia en lugar de enfrentarse a un proceso de destitución.

choices.text: Growing public and congressional accusations that he had personally engaged in illegal activity related to the Watergate break-in and cover-up.
choices.textEs: Las crecientes acusaciones públicas y del Congreso de que había participado personalmente en actividades ilegales relacionadas con el allanamiento y encubrimiento de Watergate.

items.explanation: Nixon's famous denial was made at a press conference with newspaper editors as public pressure and congressional investigations mounted over the Watergate break-in and cover-up. He was responding to growing public accusations and media reports that he had personally participated in illegal activity, including the cover-up of the Watergate burglary and the misuse of campaign funds. Option A is incorrect because the Pentagon Papers were Daniel Ellsberg's issue, not directly Nixon's criminal exposure. Option B is incorrect because the 18½-minute tape gap was discovered after this statement. Option C is incorrect because this statement preceded his resignation.
items.explanationEs: La célebre negación de Nixon se realizó en una conferencia de prensa ante periodistas mientras aumentaba la presión pública y las investigaciones del Congreso sobre el allanamiento de Watergate y el encubrimiento. Respondía a las crecientes acusaciones públicas e informes de los medios de comunicación de que había participado personalmente en actividades ilegales, incluido el encubrimiento del robo en Watergate y el uso indebido de fondos de campaña. La opción A es incorrecta porque los Papeles del Pentágono fueron el asunto de Daniel Ellsberg, no la exposición criminal directa de Nixon. La opción B es incorrecta porque el hueco de 18½ minutos en la cinta se descubrió después de esta declaración. La opción C es incorrecta porque esta declaración precedió a su renuncia.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Senate Watergate Committee has found evidence of a broad pattern of political espionage and sabotage, illegal wiretapping, and misuse of government agencies for political purposes." — Senate Watergate Committee Final Report, 1974

Which of the following best describes the significance of the Watergate scandal's findings as described in this excerpt?
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento.

"El Comité Senatorial de Watergate ha encontrado evidencia de un amplio patrón de espionaje político y sabotaje, escuchas telefónicas ilegales y uso indebido de agencias gubernamentales con fines políticos." — Informe Final del Comité Senatorial de Watergate, 1974

¿Cuál de los siguientes describe mejor la importancia de los hallazgos del escándalo Watergate según se describen en este fragmento?

choices.text: The Nixon administration had engaged in a systematic pattern of illegal political espionage and misuse of government power.
choices.textEs: La administración Nixon había incurrido en un patrón sistemático de espionaje político ilegal y uso indebido del poder gubernamental.

choices.text: Nixon was personally uninvolved in the Watergate break-in and had not participated in any cover-up.
choices.textEs: Nixon no estuvo personalmente involucrado en el robo de Watergate y no participó en ningún encubrimiento.

choices.text: The Watergate scandal was limited to a single unauthorized break-in with no broader political significance.
choices.textEs: El escándalo Watergate se limitó a un único allanamiento no autorizado sin mayor importancia política.

choices.text: Foreign governments had paid for and organized the Watergate break-in to interfere in U.S. elections.
choices.textEs: Gobiernos extranjeros pagaron y organizaron el robo de Watergate para interferir en las elecciones de EE. UU.

items.explanation: The Senate Watergate Committee's report described a systematic abuse of government power by the Nixon administration — using government agencies for political purposes, conducting illegal wiretapping, and engaging in political sabotage. This demonstrated an unprecedented abuse of executive power that threatened constitutional government. Option B is incorrect because the Committee found that Nixon personally participated in the cover-up. Option C is incorrect because the findings went far beyond a single burglary to describe a pattern of illegal conduct. Option D is incorrect because foreign governments were not implicated in the findings described.
items.explanationEs: El informe del Comité Senatorial de Watergate describió un abuso sistemático del poder gubernamental por parte de la administración Nixon —el uso de agencias gubernamentales con fines políticos, escuchas ilegales y sabotaje político—. Esto demostró un abuso sin precedentes del poder ejecutivo que amenazaba el gobierno constitucional. La opción B es incorrecta porque el Comité determinó que Nixon participó personalmente en el encubrimiento. La opción C es incorrecta porque los hallazgos iban mucho más allá de un solo robo para describir un patrón de conducta ilegal. La opción D es incorrecta porque los gobiernos extranjeros no fueron implicados en los hallazgos descritos.

Su Primer Discurso Inaugural del 20 de enero de 1981 declaró: "El gobierno no es la solución a nuestro problema; el gobierno es el problema." Esta filosofía quedó plasmada en la Ley de Recuperación Económica Tributaria de 1981, Ley Pública 97-34, que redujo la tasa marginal máxima del impuesto sobre la renta del 70 al 50 por ciento. "The Saturday Night Massacre: I ordered the firing of Special Prosecutor Cox because he refused to accept a reasonable compromise on the tapes. I had the right to do this. The President has the authority to oversee the Justice Department." — President Nixon, Statement, October 20, 1973

items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento.

«La Masacre del Sábado por la Noche: Ordené el despido del fiscal especial Cox porque se negó a aceptar un compromiso razonable sobre las cintas. Tenía el derecho de hacerlo. El presidente tiene la autoridad de supervisar el Departamento de Justicia.» — Declaración del presidente Nixon, 20 de octubre de 1973

Evalúe la justificación constitucional de Nixon para despedir al fiscal especial. ¿Cuál de los siguientes analiza mejor el principio constitucional en juego?

choices.text: Nixon's action proved that the President lacks any authority over Justice Department appointments.
choices.textEs: La acción de Nixon demostró que el presidente carece de cualquier autoridad sobre los nombramientos del Departamento de Justicia.

choices.text: The Saturday Night Massacre was primarily a violation of the Commerce Clause, which prohibits the President from interfering in independent investigations.
choices.textEs: La Masacre del Sábado por la Noche fue principalmente una violación de la Cláusula de Comercio, que prohíbe al presidente interferir en investigaciones independientes.

choices.text: Because the President technically has authority over the Justice Department, the firing was constitutionally sound and raised no concerns about the rule of law.
choices.textEs: Dado que el presidente tiene técnicamente autoridad sobre el Departamento de Justicia, el despido fue constitucionalmente sólido y no planteó ninguna preocupación sobre el estado de derecho.

choices.text: While the President has formal authority over the Justice Department, allowing the executive branch to fire its own investigators creates a conflict of interest that fundamentally undermines the rule of law.
choices.textEs: Si bien el presidente tiene autoridad formal sobre el Departamento de Justicia, permitir que el poder ejecutivo despida a sus propios investigadores crea un conflicto de intereses que socava fundamentalmente el estado de derecho.

items.explanation: Nixon's firing of Special Prosecutor Archibald Cox (the 'Saturday Night Massacre') raised the fundamental constitutional question of whether the executive branch can investigate itself. While the President technically has authority over the Justice Department, firing a prosecutor investigating the President creates an inherent conflict of interest and undermines the rule of law. Congress responded by beginning impeachment proceedings, and the public outrage demonstrated that even if technically legal, the action was seen as obstruction of justice. This illustrates the limits of formal legal authority when it conflicts with the rule of law. Option A is incorrect because Nixon was asserting authority, not abdicating it. Option B is incorrect because the constitutional issue was about the rule of law and conflicts of interest, not the Commerce Clause. Option C is incorrect because the action was widely condemned as wrong despite being technically within presidential authority.
items.explanationEs: El despido del fiscal especial Archibald Cox por parte de Nixon (la «Masacre del Sábado por la Noche») planteó la pregunta constitucional fundamental de si el poder ejecutivo puede investigarse a sí mismo. Si bien el presidente tiene formalmente autoridad sobre el Departamento de Justicia, despedir a un fiscal que investiga al presidente crea un conflicto de intereses inherente y socava el estado de derecho. El Congreso respondió iniciando procedimientos de destitución, y la indignación pública demostró que incluso si era técnicamente legal, la acción fue considerada una obstrucción a la justicia. Esto ilustra los límites de la autoridad legal formal cuando entra en conflicto con el estado de derecho. La opción A es incorrecta porque Nixon estaba afirmando autoridad, no renunciando a ella. La opción B es incorrecta porque el problema constitucional era el estado de derecho y los conflictos de intereses, no la Cláusula de Comercio. La opción C es incorrecta porque la acción fue ampliamente condenada como incorrecta a pesar de estar técnicamente dentro de la autoridad presidencial.

items.stem: Ronald Reagan's economic program reduced top marginal tax rates, cut domestic social programs, increased defense spending, and pursued deregulation. How should historians most rigorously evaluate whether Reaganomics achieved its stated objectives while simultaneously assessing its distributional effects on different income groups?

choices.text: Reaganomics largely succeeded on its own terms: the sustained economic expansion of 1983-89 validated supply-side theory by demonstrating that upper-income tax reductions generate broadly shared growth, and subsequent research confirms that the trickle-down mechanism produced improved economic outcomes across income groups.

The Reagan-era growth resulted from multiple causes — Federal Reserve success in breaking inflation, deficit spending stimulating aggregate demand, and deregulation — demonstrating that the recovery had several independent sources rather than specifically validating supply-side tax theory as the decisive variable.

Reagan's economic policies were most historically significant for their ideological legacy rather than their immediate economic performance, since the bipartisan shift from New Deal liberalism to market-oriented governance as the default framework of both parties proved far more durable than the specific outcomes of any single presidential term.

Reaganomics achieved its stated macroeconomic objectives of growth and inflation reduction but produced a distributional pattern inconsistent with the rising-tide-lifts-all-boats justification — income inequality increased substantially during the 1980s, suggesting that growth benefits were highly concentrated — requiring evaluation to distinguish between macroeconomic performance and distributional outcomes as separate analytical questions.

items.explanation: A complete evaluation of Reaganomics requires distinguishing between macroeconomic performance metrics — growth rate and inflation rate, both of which improved — and distributional outcomes — income inequality, which increased substantially by Gini coefficient measures — since the policy's political justification depended on the second claim while the evidence most clearly supports only the first.

items.stem: Which best explains the primary foreign policy challenge the United States faced following the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991?

choices.text: The United States needed to prevent former Soviet nuclear weapons from being acquired by rogue states or non-state actors.
Former Soviet republics demanding immediate NATO membership created a constitutional and strategic crisis about the alliance's expansion.
The loss of a clear superpower adversary produced a more complex threat environment, requiring new strategic frameworks to address regional conflicts, ethnic violence, and failing states.
European allies pressed the United States to reduce its military presence overseas now that the Soviet threat that had justified NATO had ended.

items.explanation: Without a clear superpower adversary, American foreign policy confronted diffuse threats: ethnic cleansing in Bosnia and Rwanda, state failure in Somalia, rogue nuclear programs in North Korea and Iraq. The strategic frameworks of containment and deterrence did not map clearly onto these challenges.

items.stem: Historians debate whether the Soviet Union's dissolution in 1991 resulted primarily from Reagan's military pressure, Gorbachev's reform initiatives, or the long-term internal structural contradictions of the Soviet system. Which explanatory framework is most analytically defensible given the available evidence?

choices.text: The Soviet collapse is best explained by the convergence of internal structural contradictions — economic stagnation, failure to compete in the Information Age, ethnic nationalist pressures, and eroding ideological legitimacy — that Reagan's military buildup may have accelerated but did not create, with Gorbachev's reforms inadvertently releasing forces that made controlled transformation impossible.

Reagan's military buildup and the Strategic Defense Initiative deserve primary credit for Soviet collapse because they forced the USSR into an arms competition its command economy could not sustain — making American strategic pressure the decisive variable that converted structural Soviet weakness into actual systemic failure.

Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika reforms were the direct and sufficient cause of Soviet collapse because they removed the coercive mechanisms on which authoritarian stability depended, revealing that the Soviet system was fundamentally held together by repression rather than solving its deep structural contradictions.

The Cold War's end primarily resulted from generational leadership change that brought pragmatic reformers to power in Moscow, demonstrating that political contingency and individual leadership decisions are more important explanatory variables than either structural or strategic factors in explaining the collapse of authoritarian states.

items.explanation: The multi-causal structural explanation is most defensible because Soviet economic stagnation, ethnic nationalism, and ideological legitimacy crisis were visible as systemic problems throughout the 1970s and 1980s — predating Reagan's buildup and existing independently of Gorbachev's choices — while Reagan's pressure and Gorbachev's reforms operated as accelerants and triggers on an already structurally compromised system.

Lea el siguiente fragmento.

«Estados Unidos contra Nixon (1974): Sostenemos que ni la doctrina de separación de poderes ni la necesidad de confidencialidad de las comunicaciones de alto nivel... pueden sustentar un privilegio presidencial absoluto e incondicional de inmunidad ante el proceso judicial.» — Presidente del Tribunal Supremo Warren Burger, Estados Unidos contra Nixon, 1974

Analice la importancia de Estados Unidos contra Nixon. ¿Cuál de los siguientes explica mejor qué estableció este fallo?

choices.text: The Court eliminated executive privilege entirely, ruling that the President has no right to keep any communications confidential.
choices.textEs: El Tribunal eliminó el privilegio ejecutivo por completo, dictaminando que el presidente no tiene derecho a mantener confidenciales ninguna comunicación.

choices.text: Executive privilege is not absolute — when criminal evidence is needed, the rule of law prevails over presidential claims of confidentiality.
choices.textEs: El privilegio ejecutivo no es absoluto —cuando se necesita evidencia penal, el estado de derecho prevalece sobre las reclamaciones presidenciales de confidencialidad—.

choices.text: The ruling applied only to the Watergate case and set no general precedent for future presidential privilege claims.
choices.textEs: El fallo se aplicó únicamente al caso Watergate y no sentó ningún precedente general para futuras reclamaciones de privilegio presidencial.

choices.text: The Court ruled that the President's communications could only be subpoenaed if they involved evidence of illegal wiretapping.
choices.textEs: El Tribunal dictaminó que las comunicaciones del presidente solo podían ser citadas judicialmente si involucraban evidencia de escuchas ilegales.

items.explanation: United States v. Nixon (1974) established that executive privilege — the President's right to keep communications confidential — is not absolute. When evidence is needed in a criminal proceeding, the rule of law prevails over executive privilege. The unanimous ruling by Chief Justice Burger (a Nixon appointee) demonstrated the independence of the judiciary and the principle that no person, including the President, is above the law. This ruling directly led to Nixon's resignation when he was ordered to release the White House tapes. Option A is incorrect because the Court upheld executive privilege in principle, just not absolutely. Option C is incorrect because the ruling applied specifically to criminal proceedings, not all information requests. Option D is incorrect because the ruling was about the limits of privilege, not about wiretapping.
items.explanationEs: Estados Unidos contra Nixon (1974) estableció que el privilegio ejecutivo —el derecho del presidente a mantener confidenciales las comunicaciones— no es absoluto. Cuando se necesita evidencia en un proceso penal, el estado de derecho prevalece sobre el privilegio ejecutivo. El fallo unánime del presidente del Tribunal Supremo Burger (un nombrado por Nixon) demostró la independencia del poder judicial y el principio de que ninguna persona, incluido el presidente, está por encima de la ley. Este fallo llevó directamente a la renuncia de Nixon cuando se le ordenó entregar las cintas de la Casa Blanca. La opción A es incorrecta porque el Tribunal sostuvo el privilegio ejecutivo en principio, solo que no de forma absoluta. La opción C es incorrecta porque el fallo se aplicó específicamente a los procesos penales, no a todas las solicitudes de información. La opción D es incorrecta porque el fallo se refería a los límites del privilegio, no a las escuchas ilegales.

Extended Response: From Containment to Collapse — Evaluating the End of the Cold War

Using your knowledge of U.S. History from the origins of the Cold War through the Modern Era, write an extended response that constructs a fully developed, evidence-based historical argument addressing the following question:

To what extent did Reagan's foreign policy strategies cause the end of the Cold War, and to what extent were the Soviet Union's internal economic and political contradictions the primary cause of its collapse?

Your response must: (1) state a clear, historically defensible thesis that addresses both sides of this causation debate and takes a position; (2) provide at least three specific pieces of historical evidence — drawn from both U.S. foreign policy actions (US.84) and Soviet internal developments — to support your argument; (3) demonstrate cross-era synthesis by connecting Reagan-era foreign policy to the containment strategy developed in the Truman era (US.59–US.62) and the détente period of the Nixon era (US.80); and (4) acknowledge and address a counterargument to your thesis.
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida: Del Contención al Colapso — Evaluando el Fin de la Guerra Fría

Usando su conocimiento de la Historia de EE. UU. desde los orígenes de la Guerra Fría hasta la Era Moderna, escriba una respuesta extendida que construya un argumento histórico completamente desarrollado y basado en evidencia abordando la siguiente pregunta:

¿En qué medida las estrategias de política exterior de Reagan causaron el fin de la Guerra Fría, y en qué medida las contradicciones económicas y políticas internas de la Unión Soviética fueron la causa principal de su colapso?

Su respuesta debe: (1) plantear una tesis clara y históricamente defendible que aborde ambos lados de este debate de causalidad y tome una posición; (2) proporcionar al menos tres piezas específicas de evidencia histórica — extraídas tanto de las acciones de política exterior de EE. UU. (US.84) como de los desarrollos internos soviéticos — para apoyar su argumento; (3) demostrar síntesis entre eras conectando la política exterior de la era Reagan con la estrategia de contención desarrollada en la era Truman (US.59–US.62) y el período de distensión de la era Nixon (US.79); y (4) reconocer y abordar un contraargumento a su tesis.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response argues — with nuance — that the Soviet collapse resulted primarily from internal structural contradictions that Reagan's policies accelerated but did not originate. Thesis: Reagan's confrontational strategy (the Reagan Doctrine, SDI, proxy wars) imposed costs on an already dysfunctional Soviet system, accelerating the timeline of collapse, but the fundamental cause was the inherent incompatibility between central planning and a technologically advancing global economy — a structural contradiction that would have produced Soviet decline regardless of American pressure. Evidence for internal Soviet causes: (1) Soviet GDP growth had stagnated from the mid-1970s — years before Reagan — as the Brezhnev-era centrally planned economy failed to adopt the microelectronics revolution that was transforming Western economies; (2) the Soviet-Afghan War (1979–89) had begun under Carter, not Reagan, and the 'Soviet Vietnam' drain on resources reflected the limits of Soviet imperial overextension, not the effect of U.S. pressure; (3) Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika were emergency reforms undertaken because Soviet leadership recognized the system's unsustainability — with or without American pressure. Evidence for Reagan's contribution: (1) SDI forced Soviet military planners to consider a multi-trillion dollar response they could not afford, diverting resources from the already-stressed civilian economy; (2) the Reagan Doctrine (funding mujahideen in Afghanistan, UNITA in Angola, Contras in Nicaragua) tied down Soviet resources in proxy conflicts; (3) the INF Treaty (1987) demonstrated that Reagan's 'peace through strength' strategy could achieve arms reductions that Nixon's détente had not. Cross-era synthesis: Reagan's strategy explicitly rejected Nixon's détente (US.79) and returned to Kennan's original containment theory (US.59) — the idea that a sustained, patient strategy of blocking Soviet expansion would eventually produce internal contradictions. In this sense, Reagan's approach completed what Truman, Eisenhower, Kennedy, and Nixon had collectively built over four decades, with Reagan accelerating the final phase. Counterargument addressed: Those who give Reagan primary credit (e.g., Peter Schweizer, 'Victory') argue that without SDI and the Reagan Doctrine, Gorbachev would have had the economic breathing room to reform the Soviet system without dismantling it — that the pressure was essential to preventing a reform that would have preserved Soviet power. A strong response engages this counterargument and explains why the structural factors were nonetheless primary.

4 - Exemplary: Clear, historically defensible thesis that takes a position on the causation debate while acknowledging complexity. Three or more specific evidence pieces drawn from both U.S. policy (SDI, Reagan Doctrine, INF Treaty) and Soviet internal factors (economic stagnation, Afghan War, glasnost/perestroika). Cross-era synthesis explicitly connects Reagan to Kennan/Truman containment (US.59–62) and Nixon détente (US.79). Counterargument is identified and substantively addressed. Writing is organized and analytically coherent.
3 - Proficient: Clear thesis with a position. Three evidence pieces, though the balance between U.S. and Soviet factors may be uneven. Cross-era synthesis present but may reference only one prior era. Counterargument noted but not fully developed.
2 - Developing: Thesis present but may lack a clear position or acknowledge only one side. Two evidence pieces. Some cross-era reference. No counterargument.
1 - Beginning: Vague or missing thesis. One evidence piece. No cross-era synthesis. No counterargument.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.
